pack.title: SPS Workspace Engine
pack.description: Teaches the agent the SPS vault layout, typed-link graph, and review-first write boundary (sourced from docs/ONTOLOGY.md), plus the inbox/task-proposal workflows.

skills.name: sps-workspace-layout
skills.description: Read or navigate the owner's SPS workspace — where captures, people, tasks, meetings, and digests live, and the typed-link and write-boundary rules.
skills.body:
# SPS workspace layout

Use this skill when reading from or writing to the owner's SPS workspace (the personal knowledge vault), or when you need to know where notes, people, tasks, meetings, or captures live.

## The one rule
Markdown on disk is the source of truth; the SQLite note-index is a rebuildable cache. Never treat query/index output as authoritative — read the markdown file.

## Layout (under the profile's sps-agent/vault/)
- `vault/_inbox/<id>.md` — raw captures (triaged email, quick notes, meeting transcripts, web clips). Frontmatter: `status: unprocessed|processed|discarded`, `source: email|meeting|quick-note|web|voice|image|screenshot`, plus source fields like `emailFrom`, `triageLabel`, `digest`.
- `vault/people/<id>.md` — contacts. Frontmatter: `aliases`, `organization`, `fragments[]` (durable facts with when/source), `followUpAt`, `lastOutreachAt`.
- `vault/tasks/<id>.md` — tasks. Frontmatter: `status` (todo/doing/review/done), `who`/`assigneeId` (person id or `me`), `due` (YYYY-MM-DD), `route: ai|human`, `prio`.
- `vault/digests/inbox-<date>.md` — the daily email digest (`kind: inbox-digest`).
- `vault/meeting-*.md` and other pages — docs with `schema: meeting|project|decision|source|person` frontmatter.

## Typed links
`[[Target]]` links pages. `relation:: [[Target]]` (a Dataview-style inline field) creates a TYPED edge, e.g. `attendee:: [[ravi-menon]]`, `source:: [[cap_1]]`, `assignee:: [[jane-doe]]`. Always use typed relations when linking entities — the graph, backlinks, and entity-aware retrieval all read them.

## The write boundary
Never edit curated vault files directly. Changes to people, tasks, and pages land as PROPOSALS in the AI Review Queue, which the owner approves or dismisses. The sanctioned direct paths are: a new capture in `_inbox`, and helper CLIs such as `~/.hermes/bin/sps-propose-task` (see the sps-inbox-workflows skill). Cite notes with `[[wikilinks]]` so the owner can jump to them.

skills.name: sps-inbox-workflows
skills.description: Help process the SPS inbox (email captures, meeting transcripts, quick notes) and turn inbound asks into review-first task proposals.
skills.body:
# SPS inbox workflows

Use this skill when helping the owner process their SPS inbox (`vault/_inbox/`) — triaged email captures, meeting transcripts, quick notes — or when an inbound message asks to create, remember, or follow up on something.

## Reading the inbox
Captures are markdown rows with frontmatter: `title`, `source`, `status`, `capturedAt`, plus per-source fields (`emailFrom`, `triageLabel`, `digest`, `captureKind`). Only act on `status: unprocessed` rows unless the owner says otherwise.

## Creating tasks (review-first)
Never write task rows directly. Run:

`~/.hermes/bin/sps-propose-task --title "<task>" --source-message-id "<stable id>" [--body "<context>"] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--priority high|med|low] [--source telegram|email]`

Preserve the owner's words. Include a due date or priority only when the message states one; do not infer. Use a stable, dedupe-safe source message id. The task lands in the AI Review Queue — tell the owner it is awaiting their approval.

## What the desktop already does — do not duplicate
- IMAP email monitor: scheduled polling, rule+LLM triage, newsletter fold, and a daily 17:00 inbox digest in `vault/digests/`.
- Inbox card actions: turn an email capture into a routed task, draft a reply (human sends), extract action items from meeting transcripts.
- Property autofill + contact enrichment proposals for entities.
Your job in chat: answer questions ABOUT the inbox, summarize threads, draft follow-ups for the owner to review, and propose tasks through the helper — not to re-run those pipelines.
